I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`, and it type-checks with the project's `tsconfig.json`. The only `tsc` errors left are in `src/module.ts`, which still imports lodash, and lodash isn't installed. I didn't run the old and new versions side by side. The behaviour matching below comes from reading the code.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 206 bytes (min+gzip) and 95 bytes of own code. I couldn't get a baseline for the original: running the size command without a file argument (it defaults to `src/module.ts`) failed because lodash isn't installed.

- **`byId`:** `keyBy` from es-toolkit with the same `(row) => row.id` callback. It gives the same result for your input range: the last row with a given id wins.
- **`totalAge`:** `sumBy` from es-toolkit. es-toolkit has no lodash-style `'age'` shorthand, so the call is now `(row) => row.age`. An empty array still returns 0.
- **`dedupeSorted`:** es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`, so I used `uniq`. On sorted input it returns the same values in the same order.

The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged, and there is no lodash import left. I didn't hand-write any replacement utilities or add other source files.
